output.name: Tiskel — The Child's Box-Kite (The Leeward Reach)
output.myth: A girl of the Holm house went down to the shingle with her brother's box-kite, bone-framed and bright with sailcloth. The wind took it from her fists and she ran after it into the tide. Tavo laughed and would not give it back. Kael cast his net all that night and hauled up only weed. Now in spring the family climbs the cliff with a second box-kite, and they fly it out over the water where she went under while Tamsi the Fish Kite watches from the north. Hesk winds the string and keeps count of the years. The kite goes up into the Leeward road and sits in the cold, a box with a tail. Ketrasa burns low to the south, over the sea that keeps drowned men, and Mesket does not weep where the children can see. The mother says the girl's hand is on the line, though no one has ever seen it. When the wind drops they reel it in, wet at the corners, glad to have it back. Then they send it up again, because the sky has not yet said no.
output.finding: Find Ketrasa, the Salt Wife's lamp, low in the south, and Tiskel hangs two fists (about 20°) due north of it in the Leeward Reach.
